newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bill to block food stamps for prison inmates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bill to block food stamps for prison inmates.

text.p: Three House members introduced a bill Monday that they said could save tens of millions of dollars by ensuring prison inmates do not get food stamps.

The measure was sparked by a General Accounting Office report that found 12,138 inmates who were counted as members of families receiving food stamps. They were identified through computer comparisons of food stamp rolls and state prison data in California, Florida, New York and Texas -- states at the top of the enrollment list -- and jail data for a major city in each of those states.
"It's an outrageous use of federal resources, enriching the households of the incarcerated," said House Agriculture Committee Chairman Bob Smith, an Oregon Republican.

Laws already deny food stamps to prisoners but the bill to be filed by Smith, Virginia Republican Bob Goodlatte and Texas Representative Charles Stenholm, the committee's top Democrat, would require states to institute a system to verify that prisoners were not participating in the food stamp programme.
If they fail to do so, they could lose a portion of their federally supplied funds for administering the programme.
The GAO estimated $3.5 million in overpayments based on the improper enrollment it identified but Goodlatte said there could be "tens of millions of dollars" in fraud nationwide.
Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Richard Lugar, an Indiana Republican, filed a similar bill March 3.
